remarks: This is a RETRY of a prior attempt (compiledAt 2026-11-04) that was flagged as thin (3 verified, 23 excluded) due to a TLS handshake reset affecting every assam.gov.in-family host. This retry re-tested every previously-excluded assam.gov.in-family URL individually this session (2026-11-17) plus several newly found candidates (labour.assam.gov.in/department-highlights/registration-and-licensing-factory, industriescom.assam.gov.in, aiinvestmentpolicy.assam.gov.in). RESULT: the condition has NOT cleared. Every assam.gov.in-family host (sewasetu., ciflabour., eodb., eservices., labour., industriescom., cib., dpns., labourcommissioner., eodbmis., industries., and the bare assam.gov.in) still fails with an immediate TLS-handshake-stage 'Recv failure: Connection reset by peer' on every attempt, including attempts with TLS1.2 forced and HTTP/1.1 forced to rule out protocol negotiation as the cause.

New diagnostic evidence gathered this retry (not available in the prior attempt): the agent-proxy's own status endpoint (curl $HTTPS_PROXY/__agentproxy/status) shows its recentRelayFailures log full of 'ws_closed_mid_exchange' and 'connect_unreachable' entries for MANY OTHER states' government domains in the same short window as these Assam attempts — e.g. rajfab.rajasthan.gov.in, www.ap.gov.in, punjab.gov.in, dic.kerala.gov.in, law.jk.gov.in, pblabour.gov.in, fabkerala.gov.in, shramsuvidha.gov.in, labour.ap.gov.in, oshwc.labour.gov.in, www.aponline.gov.in, dof.ap.gov.in. This strongly suggests the blocking condition is NOT specific to Assam or to assam.gov.in's own infrastructure, but is a broader session/egress-proxy-level condition currently affecting access to many Indian state-government web properties generally. Meanwhile, central-government sites on different infrastructure (nsws.gov.in, dgfasli.gov.in, labour.gov.in, indiacode.nic.in's own home page) continued to load fine with HTTP 200 throughout this retry, exactly as in the prior attempt.

One genuinely new and different finding this retry: https://aiinvestmentpolicy.assam.gov.in/... failed with curl exit code 60, 'SSL certificate problem: certificate has expired' — a real, verifiable server-side TLS certificate expiry, not a proxy reset. This is evidence that at least this particular assam.gov.in-family host has a genuine certificate hygiene problem of its own, independent of the session's broader connectivity issue, though it still could not be included as a verified source since content could not be retrieved without disabling certificate verification (not permitted by this session's methodology).

CONCLUSION: this retry does NOT improve on the original. Verified-source count is unchanged at 3 (NSWS home page, DGFASLI home page, DGFASLI Chief Inspectors PDF); excluded count increased slightly (from 23 to 26) only because 3 new candidate URLs were discovered and tested this retry and immediately failed for the same reason. No assam.gov.in-family URL could be verified in either attempt. Per the task instructions, this result is reported plainly as 'no better' rather than padded.

As in the prior attempt, no URL in verifiedSources was taken from a WebSearch snippet without a separate curl fetch and inspection; the DGFASLI Chief-Inspectors PDF's own content verification (pdftotext) was performed in the prior session and is still valid since the host and URL are unchanged and the host was re-confirmed reachable this session — this is noted explicitly in that entry's whatItIsNote field rather than silently re-asserted.
